name: date-card
title: Date card
summary: A tear-off calendar card: the weekday and month names looked up from string lists, and the day of the month as a number.
prompt: Make a calendar-icon style date card showing today's weekday, day number and month, like "Wed 28 Oct".
teaches: Read the date with weekDay() (1 = Monday … 7 = Sunday), calendarMonth() (1–12) and dayOfMonth()
Turn a 1-based date field into a name with textLookup over an addDataList, indexed by field - 1
Print the day number unpadded with textFromFloat whole 2, decimal 0, flags 4 (PAD_PRE_NONE)
Fit a drawing authored at the header size to any box: a variable s = min(componentWidth() / W, componentHeight() / H), a translate by half the extra space and a scale by s about the design's centre

check.describe: At 2026-10-28 the card reads Wed / 28 / Oct; at 2026-01-04 it reads Sun / 4 / Jan. Resized, the card scales to the shorter side and stays centred.

pitfalls: weekDay() and calendarMonth() are 1-based: subtract 1 to index a list
addDataList's `id` is a json2rc extension: the Java reference parser discards the list's id, so textLookup cannot name the list there and the document only converts with json2rc
A rounded header band over a rounded card: draw the band as a round rect, then a plain rect over its lower half to square the bottom corners

Canvas coordinates are pixels of the box the host gives the document, not of the header: literal coordinates sit in the top-left and get cut off when it is resized, so scale the drawing to fit (or derive positions from componentWidth()/componentHeight())
java_difference: json2rc-only: Java's addDataList drops the list id, so textLookup can't reach it (EXAMPLES_FINDINGS U4)
